newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Notionnel vols unruffled by BOF rumblings.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Notionnel vols unruffled by BOF rumblings.

text.p: Signs of monetary and foreign exchange policy discord this week within the Bank of France council have had little impact on implied volatility levels of notionnel and Pibor options, traders said on Friday.

If the debate at the highest level of the central bank were to lead to any watering down of the "franc fort" policy, they said that would be a different story, but gambling on that scenario was fraught with risks.

Eric Talleux, options trader at Paribas Capital Markets in Paris, said implied volatility on notionnel options was stable while Pibor options rose slightly after the comments calling for a stronger dollar and easing of European interest rates.

Jean-Pierre Gerard, a member of the BOF council, was quoted on Thursday as saying lack of understanding by Germany on monetary and exchange rate policy could necessitate a change in the franc-mark parity.

Gerard's comments, seeking a higher dollar against the mark and franc, followed similar remarks by fellow council member Paul Marchelli who sought interest rate cuts to boost economic growth and questioned Germany's attachment to a strong mark.
Talleux said movements in implied volatility since these comments were "nothing significant compared with the upward movement in the underlying notionnel future".

"The impact is on the absolute level of mark/Paris, but not on implied volatility," he said, adding that, in the final analysis, the Bank of France would "have to do what the government tells them" to defend the exchange rate.
"If you want to buy vol right now, you have to speculate about one movement and then nothing. So you must have good timing and be sure of what you are doing so as not to pay too much," he said.
Talleux said he expected vols to head higher next week due to uncertainty about whether the notionnel had peaked. Current vol levels were also low historically.

Talleux said implied volatility on January options on March notionnel contracts was 4.00 percent compared with a close on Thursday of 3.95 percent. February and March options stood at 4.35 (4.30 previous) and 4.50 (4.45) percent respectively.
March Pibor options implied volatility was trading at 32.5 percent, up from 31.0 percent on Thursday, and June was at 29.00 percent versus 28.5 percent.
Talleux said trading on Friday was fairly quiet.

"The only big fight today is over 129.00 on the December contract for notionnel. Some guys think that will be the absolute high top for a long time and others think it is just the first step to 130.00 maybe 131.00," he said.
A broker at a French bank in London said vols had been supported on Thursday and again on Friday by good buying of slightly out of the money calls in March notionnel.
